rag.titre: Frais pour un paiement par téléphone
rag.question: Can a card company charge an extra fee when the customer pays by phone?
rag.texte: A creditor may not impose a separate fee for telephone payments unless the payment method involves an expedited service by a customer service representative.

sources.extrait: unless such payment method involves an expedited service by a customer service representative of the creditor

rag.question: Can a 19-year-old open a credit card account on their own?
rag.texte: A card issuer may open a credit card account for a consumer less than 21 years old if the consumer submits a written application and has financial information indicating an independent ability to make the required minimum periodic payments.

sources.extrait: A card issuer may not open a credit card account under an open-end (not home-secured) consumer credit plan for a consumer less than 21 years old, unless the consumer has submitted a written application and the card issuer has: (i) Financial information indicating the consumer has an independent ability to make the required minimum periodic payments

rag.question: The card company agrees that a billing error happened. What must it do?
rag.texte: If a creditor determines that a billing error occurred as asserted, it must correct the billing error and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related charges. Additionally, the creditor must mail or deliver a correction notice to the consumer within the specified time limits.

sources.extrait: Correct the billing error and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related finance or other charges, as applicable
Mail or deliver a correction notice to the consumer.

agent.demande: What is the most a customer can owe if someone uses their lost debit card and they report it within two business days?
agent.texte: Under 12 CFR 1005.6(b), if the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution.
